newsitem.title: FRANCE: Union welcomes Fr. Telecom sell-off talks.
newsitem.headline: Union welcomes Fr. Telecom sell-off talks.

text.p: The Force Ouvriere labour union on Friday said it was pleased with the government's nomination of Michel Delebarre to lead discussions with staff and management about the possible privatisation of telecommunications operator France Telecom.

France's new leftist government is considering whether to go ahead with the plans of the previous centre-right government to partially sell France Telecom. It has suggested the sale may go ahead if employees are consulted and agree.
"Force Ouvriere PTT welcomes the government's decision to reopen the privatisation dossier of France Telecom," the union's PTT branch secretary-general Jacques Lemercier said in a statement.
He said the union had told the new government that a decision needed to be taken quickly.

It repeated the three main issues related to a decison on privatisation -- the need to safeguard a quality public service, the need for the company to develop internationally and the strengthening the unity of France Telecom.

Force Ouvriere obtained 13.9 percent of the votes at the lastest elections of staff representatives on the works council. The biggest union, Communist-led CGT with 29.3 percent, and Sud with 25.8 percent, have sofar opposed sale plans.
The CGT is organising a petition among France Telecom staff against privatisation which has so far obtained 13,000 signatures. The company has 165,000 staff.
